entries.title: Isaiah 10:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 The woe of tyrants. 5 Assyria, the rod of hypocrites, for his pride shall be broken. 20 A remnant of Israel shall be saved. 24 Judah is comforted with promise of deliverance from Assyria.

A.M. 3291. B.C. 713. Woe. 3:11; 5:8,11,18,20-22; Jer 22:13; Hab 2:6,9,12,15,19; Mt 11:21 Mt 23:13-16,23,27,29; 26:24; Lu 11:42-44,46,47,52; Jude 1:11 them. 1Ki 21:13; Es 3:10-13; Ps 58:2; 94:20,21; Da 6:8,9; Mic 3:1-4,9-11 Mic 6:16; Joh 9:22; 19:6 that write grievousness. or, to the writers that writegrievousness.

entries.content: O Assyrian. or, Woe to the Assyrian. Heb. O Asshur. Ge 10:11 the rod. 15; 8:4; 14:5,6; Ps 17:14; 125:3; Jer 51:20-24 and. or, though.

entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: when the Lord. 5,6; 14:24-27; 27:9; 46:10,11; Ps 76:10; 1Pe 4:17 I will. 16-19,25-34; 17:12-14; 29:7,8; 30:30-33; 31:5-9; 37:36-38; 50:11 Jer 50:18 punish the fruit of the stout heart. Heb. visit upon thefruit of the greatness of the heart. 9:9; Job 40:11,12; Ps 21:10; Mt 12:33; 15:19 the glory. 2:11; 5:15; Ps 18:27; Pr 30:13; Eze 31:10,14; Da 4:37

entries.title: Isaiah 10:14
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: And my. 5:8; Job 31:25; Pr 18:12; 21:6,7; Ho 12:7,8; Na 2:9-13; 3:1 Hab 2:5-11 peeped.That is, chirped, from the Latin {pipio.} We still use the term pipe to express the note of the bullfinch.

entries.content: the axe. 5; Ps 17:13,14; Jer 51:20-23; Eze 28:9; Ro 9:20,21 the rod should shake itself against them. or, a rod shouldshake them. itself, as if it were no wood. or, that which is not wood.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:24
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: O my people. 4:3; 12:6; 30:19; 46:13; 61:3; Heb 12:22-24 be not afraid. 8:12,13; 33:14-16; 35:4; 37:6,22,33-35 smite thee. 5; 9:4; 14:29; 27:7 and shall lift up his staff against thee. or, but he shalllift up his staff for thee. after the manner. Ex 1:10-16; 14:9,21-31; 15:6-10

entries.title: Isaiah 10:28
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
He is come.This is a prophetical description of the march of Sennacherib's army approaching Jerusalem in order to invest it, and of the terror and confusion spreading and increasing through the several places as he advanced; expressed with great brevity, but finely diversified. Aiath, or Ai, was situated a little east of Bethel about twelve miles north of Jerusalem; Michmash about three miles nearer, where there was a narrow pass between two sharp hills; Geba and Ramah about three miles more to the south; Gibeah a mile and a half more southward; Anathoth within three miles of Jerusalem; to the westward of which, towards Lydda, was Nob, from which place Sennacherib might have a prospect of Zion, and near which, it would appear, his army was destroyed.

Aiath. Jos 7:2; Ne 11:31 Aija. Migron. 1Sa 14:2 Michmash. 1Sa 13:2,5; 14:5,31

entries.title: Isaiah 10:30
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Lift up thy voice. Heb. Cry shrill with thy voice. Gallim. 1Sa 25:44 Laish. Jud 18:7,29 Anathoth. Jos 21:18; 1Ki 2:26; Jer 1:1; 32:8
